candidate_boundary.interpretation: Precommitted FALSUM replay on four new package/advisory records selected from the pinned full-lockfile cargo-audit findings. This is not a blind benchmark because the cargo-audit baseline predates the candidate protocol.
candidate_boundary.public_record_disjointness: The four new advisory IDs and package names are disjoint from the prior public FALSUM RustSec anchor-lang cases. They share the same RustSec advisory database source family and the same pinned ResQ application; do not call this an independent source-family holdout.

selection.rule: Freeze all four exact package/version/advisory triples reported by cargo-audit 0.22.2 in the pinned ResQ Cargo.lock replay. Do not add or remove a case after candidate execution.

candidate.range_semantics: RustSec patched and unaffected VersionReq ranges both describe versions that are not affected. If neither list contains a range, RustSec treats all versions as affected. Unsupported range syntax must abstain.
candidate.semver_reference: semver@7.8.6, restricted to explicitly supported Cargo-compatible comparator syntax
candidate.affected_functions_policy: Function metadata is preserved as context but does not establish call-site reachability. Match the package-level cargo-audit finding without claiming the affected function is used.

limits: One pinned ResQ Solana application and one RustSec database snapshot.
Four new positive package/advisory pairs; specificity on new cases is not measured.
Two previously used anchor-lang negative controls are calibration only, not held-out evidence.
cargo-audit is a credible tool reference, not human AppSec gold.
No Solana program source, deployed binary, call graph, runtime behavior, transaction, or validator is analyzed.
No ResQ maintainer adoption, independent developer reproduction, Anjoman acceptance, Telegraph ranking change, or network improvement is claimed.
